repos.title: RadixFlow: Filling Execution Bubbles in Prefix-Cached Hybrid LLM Serving
repos.paper_summary: RadixFlow is a batch-construction policy for prefix-cached serving of hybrid LLMs, where a matched prefix may need recurrent state still being produced in the same round. Its state-ready traversal blocks only the consumer of that dependency, puts it in a wait queue for the next round, and keeps scanning for independent branches that fit. The paper proves that, for a fixed round and native order, the batch contains every branch that prefix-stop would select, and that no avoidable bubble remains when readiness is monotone and no other failure stops the scan. On five hybrid models, evaluated on QuALITY and RACE candidate-scoring workloads in vLLM on A800 GPUs, it lowers mean latency by 3% to 24% and worker rounds by 11% to 44% versus the native Radix scheduler, with prefix reuse within 0.03 percentage points. On the full-attention Qwen3-8B control, latency is unchanged at 16.4 s. Ablations attribute most of the gain on larger Qwen3.5 models to traversal. The authors state that evaluation covers one generated token under fixed arrival settings, and that heavier per-round cost reduces how much of the round saving reaches latency.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Hybrid LLMs make a cache-matched branch wait for a same-round producer, and the native scan stalls behind it.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prefix-caching systems decide what state can be reused, while RadixFlow changes only which executable branches a round selects.

digest_headlines.heading: Problem Formulation
digest_headlines.headline: Batch construction must admit only branches with a matching prefix, usable state at the resume boundary, and fitting resources.

digest_headlines.heading: RadixFlow
digest_headlines.headline: RadixFlow blocks only the consumer of a same-round dependency and keeps scanning for independent work that fits.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: RadixFlow lowers mean latency and worker rounds on the hybrid models while prefix reuse stays nearly unchanged.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: A cache match is not yet a runnable branch, so schedulers should separate same-round dependencies from memory pressure.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations
digest_headlines.headline: Results cover candidate-conditioned prefill with one generated token under frozen settings, without load sweeps or production traces.

digest_headlines.heading: Ethical Considerations
digest_headlines.headline: Experiments use public benchmark inputs and public model weights, and the paper discloses assistance used in implementation and revision.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers design rationale, replay protocol, timing semantics, stream proofs, and audits of baselines and output agreement.

repos.title: Jev-ToM: Evaluating Theory of Mind in Typed Decision Models
repos.paper_summary: Jev-ToM evaluates TypeSafe Jev, a typed decision model that returns a choice and candidate probabilities, on Theory of Mind (ToM) questions. It compares five typed models and seven generative LLMs on 11,117 English questions from nine benchmarks, grouped into six capabilities. Jev scores 73.2% overall, including benchmark control questions, and ranks first or second in all six capabilities. Without controls, it scores 69.1% against GPT-3.5's 70.9%. At a descriptive 0.90 confidence cutoff, retained error ranges from 1.8% (ToMATO) to 34.9% (SimpleToM). Aligned supplied reasons raise fresh accuracy on earlier-correct cases from 96.4% to 99.0%, while swapped reasons lower it to 25.3%. On 400 behavior-prediction questions, question-only cues account for 10.75 of Jev's 14.5-point gain. Cost and observed-time comparisons favor Jev in the evaluated deployments. Limitations: English, text-only questions with supplied candidates, no full-assistant testing, possible training exposure, and exploratory confidence and reason analyses.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Assistants need repeated mental-state judgments, so this paper asks whether typed model Jev is a competitive selection component.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Earlier Jev studies cover accuracy, calibration, and adversarial sensitivity, but not cross-benchmark ToM profiles with supplied reasons.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Questions are grouped into six capability groups from nine benchmarks, with unequal source coverage across groups.

digest_headlines.heading: Results and Analysis
digest_headlines.headline: Jev ranks first or second in all six capabilities, but benchmark rankings reverse when native controls are removed.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Jev combines competitive bounded selection with favorable cost and time, but accuracy alone is insufficient for adoption.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations
digest_headlines.headline: Results cover only English text questions with supplied candidates, and the 0.90 cutoff is not a validated policy.

digest_headlines.heading: Ethical Considerations
digest_headlines.headline: The study uses existing benchmarks and annotations, and reason materials are experimental text rather than model explanations.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: Appendix lists related work, protocol, breakdowns, confidence and reason details, resource tables, and prompts.

repos.title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription
repos.paper_summary: Confucius4-R2T2 is a streaming speech recognition model built by post-training Qwen3-ASR-1.7B on about 1,500 hours of proprietary Chinese and English audio, with the pre-trained audio encoder and projector frozen. It is trained with Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) labels, a new target defined so that the emitted text never changes once output. The authors prove that LSP is monotone under the prefix order, consistent with the full-audio output, and maximal among labels that equal a whole earlier output. Training adds a Wait token where the model should defer, with teacher-generated LSP labels from 80 ms audio prefixes and noise, reverberation, and language-tag augmentation. The paper reports that streaming accuracy approaches the base model's full-context quality, with low emission lag and gains on languages not used in post-training. The stated limitations are that deployment performance and broader generalization remain open, and that the LSP label is conservative, so it biases the model toward later emission.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Revisions to emitted tokens waste downstream work, so the paper treats output stability as a hard requirement alongside accuracy and latency.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior work measures revisions, applies commit rules at inference, or trains on stable targets, while inference rules leave agreement unlearned.

digest_headlines.heading: Preliminaries
digest_headlines.headline: Streaming a full-context model is hard because timestamp targets force guesses and newly added audio can disturb earlier tokens.

digest_headlines.heading: Approach
digest_headlines.headline: Freezing the encoder, the method trains the decoder to emit a Wait token whenever the received audio does not determine the next token.

digest_headlines.heading: Training Data Construction
digest_headlines.headline: Qwen3-ASR-1.7B has the highest normalized streamability, 0.493, among the models evaluated on 1,860 Buckeye utterances.

digest_headlines.heading: Training
digest_headlines.headline: Two stages, supervised fine-tuning then reinforcement learning, train only the language decoder while the encoder and projector stay frozen.

digest_headlines.heading: Streaming Inference
digest_headlines.headline: Cache reuse, Wait-terminated decoding, bounded context and suffix verification reduce per-update cost without changing the trained model.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluations
digest_headlines.headline: R2T2 with U=1 has a total macro error of 5.76, below all three proprietary systems evaluated, and about 0.6 percentage points above full-context decoding.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Adapting a full-context model gives stable streaming recognition with transfer beyond training languages, while deployment performance remains open for further evaluation.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix defines three hindsight prefix criteria, proves their containment and coincidence relations, and treats the longest stable prefix as a learning target.

repos.title: HairDeck: Animation-Ready Stylized Hair Cards from a Single Image
repos.paper_summary: HairDeck generates the stylized hair cards of a character and the spring-bone chains that animate them, from a point cloud or a single image. Each card is one continuous token from a card VAE, and a set diffusion transformer without positional embedding denoises all card tokens of a hairstyle together with flow matching; an existence flag on each token sets the card count. A second set DiT generates the spring-bone chains from the card tokens. Training uses 36,440 CHARM hairstyles from VRoid characters, plus synthetic style augmentation and renders restyled by an image-editing model. On CHARM's 100-hairstyle test set, Chamfer distance drops from 0.0117 (CHARM) to 0.0066 and orientation error from 40.0° to 16.8°, at 1.01 s per hairstyle against 33.7 s for CHARM. On 76 rendered single-image test characters, CD is 0.0089 against 0.0139 to 0.0186 for baselines, with a 3.5% failure rate against 13.2% to 34.2%. The paper states that very short hair and alpha-textured realistic cards are outside the training data, and that no textures are generated.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Existing generators do not output the artist-placed hair cards of stylized characters, so HairDeck generates each card as one token.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Related work covers strand hair, realistic cards, stylized characters and set generation, but CHARM is the only prior stylized card generator.

digest_headlines.heading: Method
digest_headlines.headline: Each card is encoded as one continuous token, and a set diffusion transformer denoises all tokens together without positional embedding.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: On CHARM's test set HairDeck lowers Chamfer distance from 0.0117 to 0.0066 and orientation error from 40.0° to 16.8°, taking 1.01 s.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations and Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: HairDeck outputs card geometry without textures and learns only from stylized VRoid hairstyles, so short hair and realistic cards fall outside it.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists implementation settings, appearance augmentation, chain metrics, export, baseline details, and additional comparisons and results.

repos.title: Evo-RL: Iterative Robot Reinforcement Learning from Selective Experience
repos.paper_summary: Evo-RL is an iterative real-world reinforcement learning method for robot vision-language-action policies that combines human interventions with advantage-guided selection of past experience. Each round, the policy collects human corrections, keeps only the human-controlled segments of successful intervention trajectories, and trains a vision-only value model on rewards that penalize execution time and takeovers. Estimated advantages select high-advantage segments from demonstrations and successful autonomous rollouts. These segments are mixed with the corrections to fine-tune a policy initialized from π0.5. The paper also releases RW-RL-Dataset, which covers over 1,000 hours across four robot embodiments. On PiperX insertion (N=10 planned instances per unit), Evo-RL reaches 88.24% attempt success rate (ASR) versus 57.78% for RECAP, and 92.16% after a second round. On SO-101 folding (N=20 per stage), Evo-RL reaches 76.67% ASR versus 55.56% for SFT alone. Limitations: the evaluation covers two platforms with small trial counts, and each trial has a five-minute limit.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Existing methods reuse experience unevenly, so Evo-RL selects experience by estimated advantage and retains only human-controlled intervention segments.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior work pairs human corrections with offline alignment or value-guided updates, but corrective data is still poorly organized.

digest_headlines.heading: Method
digest_headlines.headline: Evo-RL initializes from demonstrations, then trains a value model on time and takeover costs and selects positive-advantage segments for fine-tuning.

digest_headlines.heading: RW-RL-Dataset
digest_headlines.headline: RW-RL-Dataset spans over 1,000 hours across four robot embodiments, with three-level semantic annotations and action-source metadata.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: On PiperX, first-round Evo-RL reaches 88.24% attempt success against 57.78% for RECAP, and a second round reaches 92.16%.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Evo-RL is concluded to outperform RECAP on PiperX, and RW-RL-Dataset is presented as a combined collection of experience.

repos.title: Intern-Decision: Efficient Multimodal Decision Making with Autoregressive Masked Language Modeling
repos.paper_summary:
Intern-Decision is a family of 0.8B, 2B, and 4B multimodal models, built on Qwen3.5 backbones, that return structured choices with candidate probabilities. Each field is a masked placeholder in an assistant JSON skeleton. Training applies cross-entropy only at placeholder positions, using the native language-model head, so all fields are scored in one causal forward pass. Inference applies a temperature-scaled softmax over each field's legal answer tokens.

The 4B model reaches 90.02% unweighted mean accuracy across seven suites, versus 88.74% for Jev v1.13.0. For a fixed 289-token, three-field request on one RTX 4090, mean latency is 44.16 ms. On a 96-case known-distribution pilot, temperature scaling lowers expected Brier from 0.628 to 0.550 and expected ECE from 0.213 to 0.089. Routing 42 low-confidence items out of 111 Jevbench-Hard items to a larger model raises accuracy from 73.87% to 87.39%.

Limitations: public Jevbench informed development, so it is diagnostic rather than held-out; no matched-data ablations isolate joint scoring or model size; generalization to large schemas is untested.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Intern-Decision proposes scoring finite agent choices in one causal pass, rather than free-form generation, for compact multimodal decision models.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Existing open decision models differ in how they score options, and Intern-Decision adds visual inputs to structured decisions.

digest_headlines.heading: Autoregressive Masked Decision Modeling
digest_headlines.headline: Each decision field gets one placeholder in an assistant output skeleton, and all fields are scored from one causal forward pass.

digest_headlines.heading: Data Construction
digest_headlines.headline: Training uses 17,880 samples and 23,500 decisions, while the 96-case calibration pilot is excluded from training and temperature fitting.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluation Results
digest_headlines.headline: Intern-Decision-4B averages 90.02% unweighted across seven suites, above Jev at 88.74%, with 44.16 ms mean latency on a fixed request.

digest_headlines.heading: Multimodal Interaction and Model Collaboration
digest_headlines.headline: Qualitative demonstrations show Intern-Decision choosing game moves, mouse actions, and browser actions inside closed control loops, without benchmark scores.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Intern-Decision is presented as a compact local decision component, with generalization to arbitrarily large schemas left unresolved.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: Appendix lists release and reproduction steps, training settings, data examples, and worked calibration cases.

repos.title: SUPRA-TEX: 3D Generation with Super-Aligned Texture
repos.paper_summary: SUPRA-Tex generates relightable 3D assets with PBR materials from a single reference image, keeping the reference's text, logos, and patterns at their visible surface locations. A 2D model built on a multimodal DiT predicts albedo and metallic-roughness maps in the reference view in one forward pass, taking 1.2 s on one H800. These maps are projected onto visible surface voxels and encoded by the frozen pretrained material VAE encoder into observation latents, which carry coverage and boundary-distance metadata. An interleaved flow transformer then generates full-surface material latents with flow matching. Observation latents serve as fixed, read-only memory, and blocks alternate between updating unobserved cells and the full surface. The 2D estimator is trained on Objaverse renders. The paper reports the best results among the evaluated methods in geometry-conditioned texturing and end-to-end generation, but the provided Table 1 excerpt cuts off before the SUPRA-Tex row, so this summary gives no SUPRA-Tex scores. Stated limitations include errors from upstream geometry or 2D material estimation, inconsistent completion across visibility boundaries, and qualitative-only failure cases with no paired two-view result.

digest_headlines.heading: 1 Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Multi-view fusion and native 3D generation both lose fine reference details, motivating a split into material estimation, alignment and completion.

digest_headlines.heading: 2 Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior texturing either fuses inconsistent multi-view predictions or conditions a native generator on implicit image features.

digest_headlines.heading: 3 Method
digest_headlines.headline: SUPRA-Tex estimates reference-view PBR maps, encodes them as fixed observation anchors, and completes the full-surface material latents.

digest_headlines.heading: 4 Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: SUPRA-Tex leads all shaded and PBR metrics in given-geometry texturing on both evaluation datasets.

digest_headlines.heading: 5 Limitations
digest_headlines.headline: Errors in upstream geometry, 2D material estimates and unobserved regions limit fidelity and asset quality.

digest_headlines.heading: 6 Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Trained only on public data, SUPRA-Tex reaches top results among evaluated methods and is competitive with commercial systems.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix gives training data, optimization, evaluation protocols, ablations, extra qualitative comparisons and a notation table.

repos.title: REMORY: Learning Residual Memory for Context Compaction
repos.paper_summary: Remory is a learned memory network that adds a bounded set of continuous soft tokens after a textual compaction summary, so a frozen LLM can approximate its continuation with the full history. The network is conditioned on the summary and emits 64 tokens per block of up to 1,024 source positions, capped at 4,096 slots. Training has two stages: reconstruction of source passages, then summary-conditioned continuation, using reverse KL against a teacher that sees the full history. On SummHay (92 queries, Qwen3.8-27B), summary plus memory raises citation F1 from 56.98 to 61.03 and joint score from 39.84 to 43.39, with coverage nearly unchanged (67.55 to 67.95), using 5.2% of raw-context positions. Within-actor agent runs improve: Qwen AutomationBench rises from 35.5 to 45.3, Terminal-Bench 2.1 from 71.9 to 76.4, and BrowseComp from 74.0 to 77.0. Limitations: the 95% bootstrap interval for the SummHay joint-score gain is [+0.74, +6.21]; Terminal-Bench and BrowseComp use one run per configuration; cost estimates exclude memory-network execution; and the first-action preference judgments do not measure outcomes.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Summaries alone may miss context needed later, so Remory adds learned memory tokens after a summary.

digest_headlines.heading: Residual Memory
digest_headlines.headline: A memory network trains soft tokens so a frozen actor matches its full-history continuation.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Residual memory raises SummHay joint score and agent scores while reducing repeated tool outputs and errors.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Remory extends summary-plus-retrieval memory with a continuous representation learned from the checkpoint.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Attribution, agent scores, and preferred next actions support the residual formulation as a bounded supplement.

repos.title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
repos.paper_summary: StreamEval is a benchmark for interactive streaming video generation, covering five tasks: avatar dialogue, avatar performance, world generation, instruction editing, and reference editing. It contains 300 scripted test cases of 15–300 s, each with initial assets, timed multimodal requests, and explicit requirements for state changes and content preservation. Ten task-specific metrics on a 0–100 scale cover four dimensions: task execution, state consistency, visual fidelity, and audiovisual coordination. Construction uses model-assisted authoring with automated and VLM-based screening, and judges are calibrated against stated false-positive and false-negative thresholds. Across 37 models, the highest task-specific scores are 36.90 for Following among seven avatar-performance models, 25.93 for Following in text-conditioned world generation, and 15.00 for Edit Success among three reference-editing models. The authors report that high visual quality and identity retention do not reliably coincide with request execution or state consistency. Limitations stated include that human judgments have not yet been collected to check agreement with the rubric, and that the editing tables show only configurations with Overall at least 5, a subset chosen after evaluation.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: StreamEval introduces a 300-case benchmark spanning five interactive streaming video tasks with ten metrics.

digest_headlines.heading: The StreamEval Benchmark
digest_headlines.headline: Each case pairs timed user inputs with explicit execution and preservation criteria, balanced across five durations.

digest_headlines.heading: System Evaluation
digest_headlines.headline: Evaluating 38 models across five tasks, Vidu S2 Editing ranks first in both editing tasks.

digest_headlines.heading: Analysis and Qualitative Results
digest_headlines.headline: A recorded reference-editing session shows retained source content but no adoption of the requested gold satin cape.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior benchmarks each cover part of streaming video, leaving no single protocol for all five StreamEval task types.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Request execution and reference-based editing remain challenging, with the highest reference Edit Success at 15.00.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists the StreamEval team, notes that author order does not reflect contributions, and acknowledges partners.

repos.title: LoongSage: A Production-Grade, High-Efficiency Agentic RL Framework for Frontier LLMs with Validated Recipes
repos.paper_summary:
LoongSage is an agent-native reinforcement learning framework for LLM post-training, built on Megatron for training and SGLang for inference, with about 14K lines of core code. Its AgentFlow layer serves agents through a Chat Completions interface and stores trajectories at the token level (Token-In, Token-Out), so sampled and trained sequences match. Black-box agents with context compaction or subagents are stored as a segment tree, and only mainline segments are trained. Three sliding-window policies bound staleness in fully asynchronous mode: no-window, window-gated (staleness at most S steps), and windowed-fifo (collection limited to one batch). TransferMesh selects a weight-transfer transport per receiver topology, such as CUDA IPC for colocated GPUs or NCCL for distributed nodes. A Teacher Manager supports multi-teacher on-policy distillation with sampled-token, top-K, full-vocabulary, and JSD estimators.

The evidence is four complete training runs, reported as steady task-reward improvement, a controlled train–inference gap, and reduced idle time. The paper does not provide a theorem. Its limitations include multi-agent credit assignment, which is left as non-trainable placeholders, and support for proprietary agent APIs, which is still under development.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Existing RL frameworks add overhead for agentic training, so the paper proposes LoongSage, built on Megatron and SGLang.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Related work argues that existing RL frameworks lack explicit support for agentic trajectories, resource sharing, and rollout–optimization boundaries.

digest_headlines.heading: The LoongSage Framework
digest_headlines.headline: The architecture uses one controller over Ray actors, token-level internal interfaces, and seven planes, with three of four placement combinations supported.

digest_headlines.heading: Key Features
digest_headlines.headline: AgentFlow stores white-box and black-box agent trajectories as token arrays and segment trees, and three sliding-window policies bound asynchronous staleness.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Four training runs show rising rewards with bounded train–inference gaps, and asynchronous execution gives a 1.35× speedup.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: The conclusion lists six contributions and plans to add Proximal Policy Optimization, Supervised Fine-Tuning, and Low-Rank Adaptation.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists author names and operational notes on hard failures, silent corruptions, and current implementation boundaries.
